title: 2 Chronicles 26:1–15
context: The people make sixteen-year-old Uzziah king. He reigns fifty-two years and does right, seeking God in the days of Zechariah, "and as long as he sought the LORD, God made him prosper." He defeats the Philistines, Arabians, and Meunim, receives tribute from Ammon, fortifies Jerusalem, builds towers and cisterns, loves farming, and equips a large army with devices for the walls. His fame spreads, "for he was marvelously helped until he was strong." This parallels 2 Kings 14:21–22 and 15:1–4, where he is called Azariah.

verses.text: All the people of Judah took Uzziah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in the place of his father Amaziah.
verses.arminianNotes: All the people of Judah make sixteen-year-old Uzziah king. Arminian readers note that the people take the initiative after the conspiracy against Amaziah, seeking stability in David's line.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that this verse parallels 2 Kings 14:21, which calls him Azariah. The two names appear in Kings and Chronicles for the same king, and these notes do not attempt to explain the difference.

verses.text: He built Eloth and restored it to Judah. After that the king slept with his fathers.
verses.arminianNotes: He builds Eloth and restores it to Judah after his father's death. Arminian readers note that Uzziah regains territory lost in earlier years, an early sign of a strong reign.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that this verse parallels 2 Kings 14:22, which reads "Elath." The recovery of this port reverses earlier losses and begins the prosperity the chapter describes.

verses.text: Uzziah was sixteen years old when he began to reign; and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Jechiliah, of Jerusalem.
verses.arminianNotes: He reigns fifty-two years; his mother is Jechiliah of Jerusalem. Arminian readers note that the long reign gave Uzziah great opportunity to lead Judah faithfully.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that this verse parallels 2 Kings 15:2, where the WEB spells his mother's name Jecoliah. The spelling difference is noted rather than resolved.

verses.text: He did that which was right in the LORD’s eyes, according to all that his father Amaziah had done.
verses.arminianNotes: He does right, as Amaziah did. Arminian readers note, consistent with the notes on 2 Kings 15:3, that the comparison is to a father whose own faithfulness was incomplete.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that this verse parallels 2 Kings 15:3. The Chronicler does not repeat the remark about the high places from 2 Kings 15:4, moving instead to Uzziah's seeking of God.

verses.text: He set himself to seek God in the days of Zechariah, who had understanding in the vision of God; and as long as he sought the LORD, God made him prosper.
verses.arminianNotes: He seeks God in the days of Zechariah, "and as long as he sought the LORD, God made him prosper." Arminian readers note that the blessing is tied to his continued seeking, a warning that blessing can be forfeited.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that the Zechariah here is a different man from the son of Jehoiada in 24:20. Uzziah's prosperity is credited to God, who blesses those who seek him.

verses.text: He went out and fought against the Philistines, and broke down the wall of Gath, the wall of Jabneh, and the wall of Ashdod; and he built cities in the country of Ashdod, and among the Philistines.
verses.arminianNotes: Uzziah fights the Philistines, breaking down the walls of Gath, Jabneh, and Ashdod, and builds cities among them. Arminian readers note the vigorous campaign of a king who acts with energy and skill.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that this account is recorded only in Chronicles. The successes against Israel's old enemies show the extent of the blessing given while Uzziah sought God.

verses.text: God helped him against the Philistines, and against the Arabians who lived in Gur Baal, and the Meunim.
verses.arminianNotes: "God helped him" against the Philistines, the Arabians of Gur Baal, and the Meunim. Arminian readers see God's active help joined with Uzziah's own efforts in battle.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note the Chronicler's emphasis on God's help. Uzziah's victories are attributed not to his own strength but to the LORD who gives success to those who seek him.

verses.text: The Ammonites gave tribute to Uzziah. His name spread abroad even to the entrance of Egypt, for he grew exceedingly strong.
verses.arminianNotes: The Ammonites pay tribute, and his name spreads to the entrance of Egypt. Arminian readers note that Uzziah's influence extends far beyond Judah, the fruit of a season of faithfulness.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that Uzziah's fame grows "for he grew exceedingly strong." The phrase prepares for the danger that strength will bring in verse 16.

verses.text: Moreover Uzziah built towers in Jerusalem at the corner gate, at the valley gate, and at the turning of the wall, and fortified them.
verses.arminianNotes: He builds and fortifies towers in Jerusalem at the corner gate, the valley gate, and the turning of the wall. Arminian readers note the wise strengthening of the city, repairing what had been broken earlier.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that the corner gate was where Joash of Israel broke the wall (25:23). Uzziah's building work restores the city's defenses after his father's defeat.

verses.text: He built towers in the wilderness, and dug out many cisterns, for he had much livestock, both in the lowlands and in the plains. He had farmers and vineyard keepers in the mountains and in the fruitful fields, for he loved farming.
verses.arminianNotes: He builds towers and cisterns in the wilderness, has much livestock, and "loved farming." Arminian readers note the care Uzziah gave to the land and its people, a picture of practical, life-giving rule.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note the warm detail that he "loved farming." Good stewardship of the land is part of the prosperity the Chronicler attributes to God's blessing.

verses.text: Moreover Uzziah had an army of fighting men who went out to war by bands, according to the number of their reckoning made by Jeiel the scribe and Maaseiah the officer, under the hand of Hananiah, one of the king’s captains.
verses.arminianNotes: Uzziah has an organized army counted by Jeiel the scribe and Maaseiah under Hananiah. Arminian readers note the careful administration of his forces, a sign of competent leadership.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that the Chronicler records the officers by name. The detail reflects the order and strength of a kingdom under God's blessing.

verses.text: The whole number of the heads of fathers’ households, even the mighty men of valor, was two thousand six hundred.
verses.arminianNotes: The heads of fathers' households, the mighty men of valor, number two thousand six hundred. Arminian readers note the structure of leadership that organized Judah's defense.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that these figures appear only in Chronicles. The numbers are recorded as part of the Chronicler's portrait of Uzziah's strength.

verses.text: Under their hand was an army, three hundred seven thousand five hundred, who made war with mighty power, to help the king against the enemy.
verses.arminianNotes: Under them is an army of three hundred seven thousand five hundred "to help the king." Arminian readers note the size of the force, showing how strong Judah had become under Uzziah.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that the army exists "to help the king against the enemy." Yet the chapter has already said where Uzziah's true help came from (26:7).

verses.text: Uzziah prepared for them, even for all the army, shields, spears, helmets, coats of mail, bows, and stones for slinging.
verses.arminianNotes: Uzziah equips the army with shields, spears, helmets, coats of mail, bows, and sling stones. Arminian readers note the thorough preparation, a king providing for those who serve under him.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note the detailed list of equipment. Uzziah's provision for his army is another mark of a reign the Chronicler presents as blessed by God.

verses.text: In Jerusalem, he made devices, invented by skillful men, to be on the towers and on the battlements, with which to shoot arrows and great stones. His name spread far abroad, because he was marvelously helped until he was strong.
verses.arminianNotes: He makes devices for shooting arrows and stones, and his name spreads, "because he was marvelously helped until he was strong." Arminian readers note that the phrase warns of what strength can do to the heart.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that the turning point is built into the verse: he was helped "until he was strong." First Corinthians 10:12 warns, "Let him who thinks he stands be careful that he doesn't fall."
